articles.title: Eka Robotics raises $150M to scale its vision-force-action model for robots
articles.summary: Eka Robotics raised $150 million in Series A funding to scale its vision-force-action model and customer deployments for dexterous manipulation robots. The company says its reinforcement-learning and simulation-based approach can help robots generalize beyond training data, including tasks such as high-speed object picking, light bulb insertion, and wire insertion.

articles.title: How to Run Underdog Saluki 27B: 2-Bit Qwen3.8-27B Tool-Calling Guide
articles.summary: MarkTechPost provides a technical guide for running Underdog Saluki 27B, a 7.9 GB two-bit quantized build of Qwen3.8-27B, and comparing it with ISTA-DASLab’s GSQ-RCO version in stock llama.cpp. The guide focuses on GGUF file differences, memory and speed on a single GPU, and tool-calling performance using a seeded 120-task Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard evaluation.
articles.advisor_relevance: The article is technically focused but points to an important AI adoption theme: smaller, heavily quantized models may preserve useful tool-calling capabilities while reducing memory and hardware requirements. This could support broader local or cost-efficient AI deployment over time, though the piece does not provide direct commercial adoption, revenue, or capex implications.

articles.title: Putting a Dollar Figure on Compressed Air Blow-Off
articles.summary: The article explains that compressed-air blow-off in factories can be a costly energy use because compressors convert most electrical energy into heat and often run longer or at higher pressure than needed. It outlines a basic cost calculation for blow-off, identifies leaks and pressure mismatch as common losses, and suggests fixes such as leak repair, solenoid valves, engineered nozzles, and blower-driven air knife systems where appropriate.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is not directly an AI article, but it is relevant to industrial automation and manufacturing cost control. It highlights how plants can reduce electricity usage and operating expense through better measurement, maintenance, and equipment substitution, with potential read-throughs to industrial efficiency suppliers rather than AI infrastructure or software adoption.

articles.title: Cognition Open-Sources an Agent Plugin that Helps Secure Systems against Recent Cybersecurity Threats
articles.summary: Cognition released the Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin, an MIT-licensed set of three agent skills designed to inventory, patch, and test PHP, Node.js, and self-managed GitLab deployments affected by recent critical remote code execution flaws. The plugin can open one pull request per repository, positioning the agent as a practical tool for security remediation workflows.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a concrete example of AI agents moving beyond code generation into operational software maintenance and cybersecurity response. For advisors, it supports the broader thesis that AI may reshape developer tooling, security workflows, and enterprise software productivity, though the direct investment implications are limited by the narrow scope and lack of commercialization details.
